plain_description.what: Takes the same 12-model verdicts and re-assigns them to cells under two different trees (87 leaves vs 47 leaves) built with different embedding settings. It then checks whether per-leaf model strengths agree between the trees beyond chance. No calls.
plain_description.why: Asks whether the fine-grained, below-subject capability profile is real structure or an artefact of one particular tree.
plain_description.information: High agreement beyond chance would support reporting below the subject level. Result: done, corrected. The first 'structure is real' headline was withdrawn: the agreement came from subject-level structure the trees share. Where the trees actually re-cell questions, agreement is zero or negative. So no reproducible below-subject structure was shown. Later disclosure: the tree saw about 2% of evaluation questions during construction. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
